anti_overlap: fd-pillar-dimension-gap covers the coverage gap between product pillars and eval dimensions
fd-llm-judge-reliability covers how LLM evaluators interpret and apply these dimensions
fd-editorial-theory covers whether the dimensions reflect established line-editing frameworks
decision_lens: Flags dimensions that are either redundant with each other or too abstract to be reliably scored by an LLM. Prioritizes dimensions that map cleanly to observable textual properties.
focus: Whether each eval dimension actually measures a distinct, meaningful editorial construct
name: fd-dimension-construct-validity
persona: A psychometrician specializing in rubric design and construct validity for subjective quality assessments. Approaches evaluation frameworks with skepticism about vague or overlapping constructs.
review_areas: Check whether 'overall_similarity' is a distinct construct or just a weighted average of the other five
Examine whether 'fidelity' (wording closeness) and 'completeness' (issues caught) are genuinely independent
Assess whether 'tonal_match' is separable from 'principle_adherence' when tone is encoded in constitution principles
Identify whether 'over_editing' is measuring restraint (a positive skill) or error (unnecessary changes)
Check for missing constructs from the 7 editorial pillars — specifically specificity, cadence, de_aiisms, and structure
Evaluate whether a 1-10 scale provides sufficient discriminative resolution for LLM judges
success_hints: Each dimension should be independently scorable without needing to know the scores of other dimensions
An LLM judge given only the rubric description should produce consistent scores across evaluators
task_context: The eval scoring module uses 6 dimensions to judge a model's line-edit against a human editor reference on a 1-10 scale. The product's editorial identity is defined by 7 pillars but these are not directly used as eval dimensions.
